second_order: turning familiar Isaac formats into April Fools tricks
theme_note: These codes use recurring comparisons, familiar items, and ordinary game forms to stage April Fools tricks; what varies is whether people author the trick, answer it seriously, or make a one-off mod.

These codes bring people into the build with calls, coordinates, links, placement instructions, and practical access help; recruits range from newcomers asking what to do to contributors already placing pixels.

These codes propose, start, complete, or choose visible parts of the shared figure—from its body and name to items, wings, characters, and small details; additions vary from coordinated builds to playful proposals that never hold.

second_order: rallying to save Isaac from the Void and griefers
theme_note: These codes raise alarms, call for protection, repair after threats, and redirect damage into new work; the named threat varies between the Blue Corner, the Void, bots, stray pixels, and uncoordinated griefers.

second_order: making room with neighbors through truces and borders
theme_note: These codes negotiate coexistence, protection, shared overlays, border pixels, mutual repair, and refusals to overwrite others; relations vary from Rainbow Road protection and HoS truces to unanswered help offers and perceived broken promises.

second_order: asking and explaining how r/place works
theme_note: These codes turn newcomer questions into explanations of the shared canvas, its placement delay, and its mixture of creation, defense, and destruction; some answers are practical and others retrospective.

second_order: celebrating Isaac as a shared win
theme_note: These codes admire progress, say 'we did it,' praise survival, claim small contributions, and finally call the finished drawing a won run; celebration ranges from premature completion claims to post-closure victory.

second_order: keeping planned pixels from being erased
theme_note: These codes share templates, explain intended changes, correct mistaken cleaning, divide work, and ask for coordination so additions are not read as vandalism; some repairs succeed briefly while tape, feet, wings, and glasses are repeatedly undone.

second_order: working out what April Fools changed
theme_note: These codes ask about and explain strange headers, Northernlion memes, character sprites, daily runs, and the timing of reversions; responses vary between confusion, recognition, reassurance, and annoyance.

second_order: making Isaac jokes out of the canvas
theme_note: These codes turn the live figure, nearby art, and proposed additions into jokes such as Angels versus Devils, Meat Boy in the Void, snek, green Isaac, and a diaper; the practice is playful commentary on the canvas rather than ordinary building alone.

second_order: flooding the subreddit with Egg and Northernlion
theme_note: These codes perform the room's own April Fools takeover through Egg and Northernlion posts, search-result campaigns, chants, altered names, flair demands, and mock reverence; the form varies from repetition to deliberate extension into ordinary posts.

second_order: pushing back on takeovers and territorial seriousness
theme_note: These codes complain about the continuing Egg flood, dismiss posts or proposals, object to screenshot saturation, and criticize defensive territorial seriousness; the objections target different excesses rather than forming one alternative project.

second_order: replaying and recounting who did what
theme_note: These codes use timelapses and final-result discussion to remember threats, lost additions, individual pixels, neighboring art, and visual changes; accounts vary between credit, lament, explanation, and criticism.

second_order: keeping r/place Isaac alive after the canvas
theme_note: These codes redraw and remake the figure, recruit flair and sidebar homes, fold mourning into the Item Workshop, and propose game content as a token of the room's work; preservation varies between art, subreddit memory, and hoped-for implementation.

These codes recruit people to rebuild and defend Isaac on the replacement canvas and propose marking it with the subreddit name; the calls return to Reddit while the placements themselves remain off-platform.
